hero.title: Your blockchain capstone: from problem to defended project
hero.subtitle: Choose a problem, write testable stories, design with a complete reference contract, build test-first, review your own security, deploy to a test network, document and defend. Every task is checked and explained.
hero.outcomeLine: After this course you have one complete, tested, documented and honestly described blockchain project and the story to present it.

assessment: Finish the required labs in each module: they are checked automatically and explained when something is missing.
Pass each module quiz (70% or more). Short tests inside the lessons give instant feedback.
Write the capstone report and pass the final assessment.

faq.q: Does the platform build or run my project?
faq.a: No. The labs check your plans, calculations and writing. You build, test and deploy in your own tools on a test network.

faq.q: Do I have to use the credential registry?
faq.a: No. It is a reference you can follow or adapt. Any well-scoped project of your own works, as long as you can test and defend it.

faq.q: Is this a security audit or a job guarantee?
faq.a: No. Your self-review is good practice but not a professional audit, and no course guarantees employment.

activities.title: Estimate effort and check the plan fits
activities.objective: Adjust task estimates for risk, compare them with the time you have and decide whether to cut scope.
activities.scenario: A capstone has five task groups. Each estimate is multiplied by a risk factor. You have 10 hours a week for 12 weeks. (A teaching model.)
steps: In D2 work out the adjusted hours: estimate times risk factor. Fill down to D6.
In B11 add up the adjusted hours.
In B12 work out the hours available.
In B13 work out the shortfall, never below zero.
In B14 show Cut scope if there is a shortfall, otherwise Fits.
In B15 work out the weeks needed at your weekly hours, rounded up.

checks.label: D2 is the adjusted hours
D4 is the adjusted hours
B11 is the total
checks.hint: =SUM(D2:D6)

checks.label: B12 is the hours available
B13 is the shortfall
B14 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(B13>0,"Cut scope","Fits")

checks.label: B15 is the weeks needed
checks.hint: =ROUNDUP(B11/B8,0)

activities.title: Track progress honestly
activities.objective: Compare planned and actual hours, see how far behind you are and decide what to do.
activities.scenario: You planned 62 hours across six weeks and logged what really happened. (A teaching model.)
steps: In D2 work out the difference: actual minus planned. Fill down to D7.
In B9 add up the planned hours.
In B10 add up the actual hours.
In B11 work out the progress as a percentage of the plan.
In B12 show Behind: cut scope or add time if progress is below 80, otherwise On track.

activities.title: What would it cost to run for a year?
activities.objective: Estimate running costs and cost per user so your documentation can be honest about sustainability.
activities.scenario: If the project were run for real, it would need hosting, an RPC provider, monitoring, a domain and a one-off security review. (A teaching model in rupees.)
steps: In B9 add up the monthly running costs (hosting, RPC provider and monitoring).
In B10 work out the yearly running cost: monthly times 12 plus the domain.
In B11 add the one-off review to get the first-year total.
In B12 work out the first-year cost per user.
In B13 show Seek funding or reduce scope if the cost per user is above 300, otherwise Affordable.

activities.title: Final project: write your capstone report
activities.objective: Write the final report of a complete blockchain capstone: what you built, why, how, how you checked it and what remains.
activities.scenario: Write the capstone report for a project you have designed (the credential registry is a fine choice). It is the document a reviewer reads before your defence.
steps: Add a Heading 1 with the project name and 'capstone report'.
Add Heading 2 sections: Summary, Problem and users, Requirements, Architecture, Implementation, Security and testing, Deployment and operations, Results, Limits and future work.
Under Requirements write a numbered list of at least five requirements.
Under Security and testing mention a threat model, tests and the fact that it has not been audited.
Under Deployment and operations mention the test network and the verified source code.
Under Limits and future work be honest about what the project cannot do.
Keep it between 420 and 860 words.
